name: Laos

findings.controller: China Great Wall Industry Corporation; APMT (PRC state contractors)
findings.local_actor: Lao government (NAST/MTC); Lao Asia Pacific Satellite Co.
findings.summary: LaoSat-1 communications satellite, built by a PRC state space contractor under a ~$259M EPC deal and financed by China Exim loans, was delivered in orbit in 2016 and is run by a Lao-PRC joint venture.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: PRC-built bus, PRC state lender and PRC state co-owner of the operating JV; exact shareholding not stated in sources. Value is the EPC contract figure (AidData), not a verified outturn. Audit 2026-10-22: Contractors per AidData are China Great Wall Industry Corporation and APMT, not CAST.

findings.summary: Lao Telecom signed network-expansion contracts and a strategic cooperation MoU, including a 5G alliance, with Nokia Shanghai Bell for LTE products, IP and services; value undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Nokia Shanghai Bell is a Nokia-controlled JV with a PRC state co-owner; coded third (Nokia, Finland) as controller, but the PRC minority stake is material. No source identified LTC's or Unitel's current 5G RAN/core vendor.

findings.summary: Laos and a Chinese firm agreed to establish a national satellite data management and service centre in Vang Vieng, including a BeiDou ground station; financing undisclosed, construction not reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Source is a business-council news digest (S4) and likely relays Lao state media; no primary confirmation seen.

findings.summary: The ministry signed an MoU with a Lao IT firm to run a six-month feasibility study for a National Data Centre, Government Data Exchange System and groundwork for a national cloud.
findings.analyst_inference: Vientiane Times is state-owned, so S4. Underlying hardware/cloud vendor not named; the domestic pole describes only the project controller.

findings.controller: Silicon Tech Park (Lao) Sole Co., Ltd.
findings.local_actor: National Data Center, Ministry of Technology and Communications
findings.summary: MoU for a feasibility study on green-powered AI infrastructure: an AI Innovation Center pilot and a proposed 150-hectare AI special economic zone in Vientiane; no value or construction reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: the company is Lao-registered but its ultimate ownership is not stated, so controller jurisdiction is unknown.

findings.controller: ALO Technology Group with China-Lao Information Communication Centre / China-ASEAN Information Harbor
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Technology and Communications; National University of Laos
findings.summary: Laos launched a Lao National Large Language Model project led by ALO Technology Group with Chinese partners; an initial prototype is being trialled while Lao-language datasets are collected. Base model not named.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: base model and ALO's nationality are not stated. Analyst inference: the named PRC-linked partners make a PRC-origin base model plausible but unverified.

findings.controller: Ministry of Technology and Communications (vendor not named)
findings.summary: The technology minister announced a Lao AI platform, a large language model trained on official Lao-language data for translation, writing and news analysis; still being improved. No vendor or base model named.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: no developer or base model named. May be the same effort as LAO-006 at a later stage; sources do not link them. Coded tier 2 because the platform is described as still in improvement, not at scale.

findings.local_actor: Presidents Office; Lao Party Central Committee Office
findings.summary: Under an 'In Laos For Laos' programme, Huawei Laos supplied IT equipment to upgrade office systems at the Presidents Office and Party Central Committee Office, and offered digital-economy consulting.
findings.analyst_inference: Source is a sponsored advertorial in state media. Instrument tier 2 because scale and contract terms are undisclosed.

findings.summary: A Korean manufacturer and a Lao partner donated a small 360-degree CCTV system worth about $51,000 to the Ministry of Public Security for road safety and city security.
findings.analyst_inference: Small donation (five cameras); coded tier 2 as pilot-scale. Not evidence of a city-wide safe-city system.

silicon.null_reason: search budget spent on networks, facilities, models and applications; no accelerator purchase surfaced incidentally

power.null_reason: one search found only crypto-mining power suspensions (not AI-related); hydropower is pitched for data centres but no dedicated AI supply deal found

corrections.note: Migrated to spec v0.2 (scale, reversal_reason, still_current, builder/financier, base model, opened flags; corroboration recomputed on opened sources) and audit corrections applied.

research_gaps: Current RAN/core vendor for Lao Telecom, Unitel (Viettel) and ETL 4G/5G networks; Huawei and ZTE presence is unconfirmed by S1/S2 sources.
Base model and ownership behind the Lao National LLM (ALO Technology Group, China-ASEAN Information Harbor) and whether the July 2026 MTC Lao AI platform is the same system.
Shareholding of Lao Asia Pacific Satellite Co. (LaoSat JV) and status of the Vang Vieng satellite data centre with BeiDou ground station.
Who builds and operates the National Data Centre / national cloud after the 2025 feasibility MoUs, and on which vendor stack.
Any Huawei or PRC safe-city / surveillance procurement by the Ministry of Public Security; none found in S1-S3 sources.
Nearly all Laos evidence is Lao state media (S4); S1/S2 confirmation is needed before any finding is relied on.
